The annotation processing loop will fail to correctly handle multiple `container_file_citation` annotations because string indices become invalid after the first replacement\.


<details>
<summary>View Details</summary>
<!-- PATCH_DETAILS_PLACEHOLDER -->

### Analysis
## Multiple container\_file\_citation annotations produce incorrect text replacements

**What fails\:** The `OpenaiResponsesText` component incorrectly handles multiple `container_file_citation` annotations in a single message because it processes annotations sequentially while using string indices that become invalid after each replacement\.

**How to reproduce\:** A single text response with two file citations\:

*   Text\: \"Result\: \[file1\] and \[file2\] done\"
*   Annotation 1\: start\_index\=8\, end\_index\=15 \(\"\[file1\]\"\)
*   Annotation 2\: start\_index\=20\, end\_index\=27 \(\"\[file2\]\"\)

After processing Annotation 1\, the string becomes \"Result\: \[URL\-\.\.\.\] and \[file2\] done\"\, which shifts all subsequent character positions by \~15 characters\. When processing Annotation 2 at the original indices \[20\, 27\]\, it now points to the wrong position and corrupts the output\.

**Result\:** Text becomes corrupted with incorrect replacements\: \"Result\: \[URL\-\.\.\.\] and \[URL\-\.\.\.\]\" with misaligned brackets\/text

**Expected\:** Both annotations should be correctly replaced with their respective URLs while maintaining text integrity

**Fix applied\:** Sort annotations in descending order by `start_index` before processing\. By processing from the end of the string backwards\, modifications to the string don\'t invalidate indices of annotations that haven\'t been processed yet\.

**References\:**

*   [OpenAI Community discussion on handling multiple citations](https://community.openai.com/t/how-to-handle-file-citations-with-the-new-responses-api/1146454) mentions developers experiencing \"letters and words getting jumbled\" when processing multiple citations \- the exact symptom this bug produces
*   Azure OpenAI Responses API documentation shows that `annotations` is an array field\, confirming multiple annotations per response are possible

</details>

```suggestion
                      annotations: [...ongoingAnnotations],
```

The `ongoingAnnotations` array is passed by reference \(not copied\) when creating the `text-end` event\. This causes a bug where if another message arrives and clears the array before the consumer processes the `text-end` event\, the annotations will appear empty\.


<details>
<summary>View Details</summary>
<!-- PATCH_DETAILS_PLACEHOLDER -->

### Analysis
## Array reference causes annotations to be lost in text\-end event

**What fails\:** In `OpenAIResponsesLanguageModel.doStream()`\, when multiple messages are streamed\, annotations from the first message become empty in the `text-end` event if a second message arrives before the event is consumed\.

**How to reproduce\:**

```
Stream a request with multiple messages where the first message contains annotations. The second message will arrive and clear the `ongoingAnnotations` array before the first message's `text-end` event is fully processed, causing the array reference to point to an empty array.

This occurs in the TransformStream's synchronous transform() method where:
1. Message 1's text-end event is created with direct reference to ongoingAnnotations (line 1474)
2. Message 2 arrives and immediately clears the array with splice() (line 984)
3. The queued text-end event now references an empty array
```

**Result\:** The `text-end` event\'s `providerMetadata.openai.annotations` field is empty even though annotations were present in the stream\.

**Expected\:** Each `text-end` event should contain the annotations that were present for that specific message\, regardless of when subsequent messages arrive\.

**Fix\:** Create a copy of the array when passing it to the event using the spread operator\: `annotations: [...ongoingAnnotations]` instead of `annotations: ongoingAnnotations` \(line 1474 of openai\-responses\-language\-model\.ts\)

</details>

body:
I spent some time investigating this and concluded that the previous shape no longer matches the current behavior of the OpenAI APIs. This might be the result of a breaking change OpenAI made in the past.

Concretely:

- `file_citation` no longer has `start_index`.
- `file_citation` no longer has `end_index`.
- `file_citation` no longer has `quote`.
- `container_file_citation` no longer has `index`.

Because these properties were defined as `nullish` in the AI SDK types, our tests still passed even after OpenAI removed them, so it was hard to notice the breaking change on our side.

You can see the current shape in the official docs and the OpenAI Node definitions:

- `file-citation` API Reference
  https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses/object#responses-object-output-output_message-content-output_text-annotations-file_citation
- OpenAI Node annotations definitions  
  https://github.com/openai/openai-node/blob/0732dd64626ae4029ad2813e5116b8c56209548d/src/resources/responses/responses.ts#L4547-L4652

Also, if you look at the fixtures in this repository (`openai-code-interpreter-tool.1.chunks.txt` and `openai-file-search-tool.1.chunks.txt` under `fixtures`), you’ll see that these properties are not present in the real data we captured. The tests still pass with the updated types, so we’re not deviating from what OpenAI actually returns.

On a more opinionated note: I think the `nullish` option is very useful in many parts of the AI SDK, but for annotations specifically it may have been hiding these upstream breaking changes. Personally, I’d prefer stricter types here so that we notice and react quickly when OpenAI changes the annotation shape.

That said, if you still prefer these properties to be marked as nullish for your intended use, I’m happy to add them back and reopen the PR with that adjustment.

The injected synthetic tool is hard-coded as `name: 'json'`, but `LanguageModelV4FunctionTool.name` is required to be unique within a call. If the user already supplied a tool named `json`, this will create duplicates and may cause provider-side request rejection or ambiguous tool routing.

Before injecting, detect an existing `json` tool name and either (1) pick a reserved unique name (e.g. `__ai_sdk_json`), updating the response extraction logic accordingly, or (2) throw/emit a clear warning telling the user to rename their tool.
author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer

body:
In streaming mode, `json` tool call deltas are emitted as `text-*` events, but the stream’s `finishReason` remains whatever Groq reports (commonly `"tool_calls"`). This has the same effect as non-streaming: downstream consumers may treat the response as a tool-call step rather than a completed text step.

Consider mirroring Anthropic/Bedrock: track whether the `json` response tool was used (and whether any non-`json` tool calls were present), and map the unified finishReason to `stop` for the json-tool-only case before emitting the final `finish` event.
author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer

body:
Same tool-name uniqueness concern as Groq: the synthetic fallback tool is injected as `name: 'json'` without checking for collisions with user-supplied tools. Since tool names must be unique per call, this can break requests if the user already has a `json` tool.

Recommend guarding against duplicates (rename synthetic tool to a reserved unique name, or emit a clear error/warning).


The `toImageModelV3File` function inefficiently calls `convertDataContentToUint8Array` twice on the same input data\, which could be expensive for large image files\.


<details>
<summary>View Details</summary>
<!-- PATCH_DETAILS_PLACEHOLDER -->

### Analysis
## Double conversion of data content in toImageModelV3File function causes inefficient base64 decoding

**What fails\:** The `toImageModelV3File` function in `packages/ai/src/generate-image/generate-image.ts` \(lines 319\-336\) calls `convertDataContentToUint8Array(dataContent)` twice on the same input\, causing unnecessary decoding operations for large image files\.

**How to reproduce\:**

```typescript
// Call toImageModelV3File with a base64-encoded image
const base64Image = 'iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAACklEQVR4nGMAAQAABQABDQottAAAAABJRU5ErkJggg==';
toImageModelV3File(base64Image);
```

**What happens\:** The function executes\:

1.  First call on line 329\: `data: convertDataContentToUint8Array(dataContent)`
2.  Second call on line 332\: `convertDataContentToUint8Array(dataContent)` \(inside detectMediaType call\)

This means base64 strings are decoded twice\, and ArrayBuffers are converted twice\, wasting CPU cycles and memory\.

**Expected behavior\:** The data should be converted once and reused for both the `data` property and the `detectMediaType` function call\.

**Implementation\:** Store the result of `convertDataContentToUint8Array(dataContent)` in a variable \(`uint8Data`\) and reuse it in both locations\, reducing the conversion from 2 calls to 1 call per image file\.

</details>

### Analysis ## Duplicate version headers in private package CHANGELOG violates changelog standards **What fails\:** The CHANGELOG\.md for `packages/rsc/tests/e2e/next-server` \(a private test package with `"version": "0.0.0"`\) contains 215 identical `## 0.0.1` version headers instead of unique version numbers\. This occurs because Changesets generates changelog entries for dependency updates without incrementing the version for private packages\. **How to reproduce\:** ```bash # Check the private package's package.json cat packages/rsc/tests/e2e/next-server/package.json | grep -A1 '"private"' # Shows: "private": true, "version": "0.0.0" # Count the duplicate headers grep -c '^## 0\.0\.1$' packages/rsc/tests/e2e/next-server/CHANGELOG.md # Shows: 215 identical headers ``` **Result\:** According to the [Keep a Changelog standard](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/)\, each version should have a unique header\, and \"versions and sections should be linkable\.\" Having 215 identical headers violates this standard and breaks changelog parsing tools\. **Expected behavior\:** Private packages \(marked `"private": true`\) should not have their CHANGELOGs generated or maintained by Changesets\, as they are not published and don\'t follow semantic versioning\. Per [Changesets documentation](https://github.com/changesets/changesets/blob/main/docs/config-file-options.md)\, the `privatePackages` configuration option should be set to disable changelog generation for private packages\. **Fix\:** 1. Configure `.changeset/config.json` with `"privatePackages": { "version": false, "tag": false }` to prevent Changesets from generating CHANGELOGs for private packages 2. Remove the malformed CHANGELOG\.md file for this private test package


Incomplete optional chaining will cause a runtime error if `providerOptions` exists but doesn\'t have a `google` property\.


<details>
<summary>View Details</summary>
<!-- PATCH_DETAILS_PLACEHOLDER -->

### Analysis
## Incomplete optional chaining in convertToGoogleGenerativeAIMessages causes runtime TypeError

**What fails\:** The `convertToGoogleGenerativeAIMessages()` function throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'thoughtSignature')` when processing assistant message parts with `providerOptions` that doesn\'t contain a `google` key\.

**How to reproduce\:**

```javascript
convertToGoogleGenerativeAIMessages([
  {
    role: 'assistant',
    content: [
      {
        type: 'text',
        text: 'Regular text',
        providerOptions: { anthropic: { something: 'value' } }, // google key missing
      },
    ],
  },
]);
```

**Result\:** TypeError\: Cannot read properties of undefined \(reading \'thoughtSignature\'\) at line 84

**Expected behavior\:** Should handle the case gracefully where `providerOptions` exists but doesn\'t have a `google` property\, returning `undefined` for `thoughtSignature`

**Root cause\:** Line 84 uses incomplete optional chaining\: `part.providerOptions?.google.thoughtSignature`\. When `providerOptions` exists but `google` is undefined\, the optional chaining short\-circuits and returns `undefined`\, then the code attempts to access `.thoughtSignature` on that `undefined` value\.

**Fix applied\:** Changed line 84 to use complete optional chaining on both accesses\:

*   Before\: `part.providerOptions?.google.thoughtSignature`
*   After\: `part.providerOptions?.google?.thoughtSignature`

Also updated the ternary operator\'s right side for consistency\:

*   Before\: `String(part.providerOptions.google.thoughtSignature)`
*   After\: `String(part.providerOptions.google?.thoughtSignature)`

This follows the defensive programming pattern already established in the codebase and matches the type definition of `ProviderOptions` as `Record<string, JSONObject>`\, which allows any provider\-specific keys\.

</details>

The `start_index` and `end_index` fields are required in the streaming chunk schema for `url_citation` annotations\, but existing test data and potentially older API responses don\'t include them\, causing validation failures\.
View Details
📝 Patch Details ```diff diff --git a/packages/openai/src/responses/openai-responses-api.ts b/packages/openai/src/responses/openai-responses-api.ts index 5318ae298..baa9a4f72 100644 --- a/packages/openai/src/responses/openai-responses-api.ts +++ b/packages/openai/src/responses/openai-responses-api.ts @@ -559,8 +559,8 @@ export const openaiResponsesChunkSchema = lazySchema(() => annotation: z.discriminatedUnion('type', [ z.object({ type: z.literal('url_citation'), - start_index: z.number(), - end_index: z.number(), + start_index: z.number().nullish(), + end_index: z.number().nullish(), url: z.string(), title: z.string(), }), @@ -687,8 +687,8 @@ export const openaiResponsesResponseSchema = lazySchema(() => z.discriminatedUnion('type', [ z.object({ type: z.literal('url_citation'), - start_index: z.number(), - end_index: z.number(), + start_index: z.number().nullish(), + end_index: z.number().nullish(), url: z.string(), title: z.string(), }), ```
### Analysis ## url\_citation schema validation fails for streaming chunks without start\_index and end\_index **What fails\:** The `url_citation` schema in `packages/openai/src/responses/openai-responses-api.ts` \(lines 561\-566 and 689\-694\) requires `start_index` and `end_index` fields\, but test data at line 4970 in `openai-responses-language-model.test.ts` provides `url_citation` annotations without these fields\, causing Zod schema validation to fail\. **How to reproduce\:** ```javascript const { z } = require('zod/v4'); const urlCitationSchema = z.object({ type: z.literal('url_citation'), start_index: z.number(), // Required end_index: z.number(), // Required url: z.string(), title: z.string(), }); // Test data without start_index/end_index (from line 4970) const testData = { type: "url_citation", url: "https://example.com", title: "Example URL" }; urlCitationSchema.parse(testData); // Throws validation error ``` **Result\:** Validation error with messages\: * `start_index: Invalid input: expected number, received undefined` * `end_index: Invalid input: expected number, received undefined` **Expected\:** Should pass validation\. The `file_citation` and `container_file_citation` schemas use `.nullish()` for `start_index` and `end_index` to maintain backward compatibility with API responses that may not include these fields\. The `url_citation` schema should follow the same pattern to support streaming chunks that only contain annotation type\, url\, and title\. **Fix\:** Changed `start_index` and `end_index` in `url_citation` schema to `.nullish()` \(making them optional\/nullable\) to match the pattern used in other citation types and align with the actual API response format shown in the test data\.

```suggestion
          effort: huggingfaceOptions.reasoningEffort,
```

Redundant condition check in reasoning effort configuration\: the inner condition checking `huggingfaceOptions?.reasoningEffort != null` is unnecessary since it\'s already verified in the outer spread operator\.


<details>
<summary>View Details</summary>
<!-- PATCH_DETAILS_PLACEHOLDER -->

### Analysis
## Redundant inner condition check in reasoning effort configuration

**What fails\:** `HuggingFaceResponsesLanguageModel.getArgs()` in `packages/huggingface/src/responses/huggingface-responses-language-model.ts` \(lines 140\-146\) contains a redundant nested condition check that evaluates the same boolean expression twice unnecessarily

**How to reproduce\:**

```typescript
// Existing code with redundant inner condition:
...(huggingfaceOptions?.reasoningEffort != null && {
  reasoning: {
    ...(huggingfaceOptions?.reasoningEffort != null && {  // ← REDUNDANT
      effort: huggingfaceOptions.reasoningEffort,
    }),
  },
}),
```

**Result\:** When `huggingfaceOptions?.reasoningEffort` is truthy\, the outer condition evaluates to true and spreads the object containing the reasoning configuration\. The inner spread operator then evaluates the identical condition again\, which will always be true at that point \(since if it were false\, the outer condition would have prevented execution\)\. This creates dead code that serves no purpose\.

**Expected behavior\:** The inner condition check should be removed since it\'s guaranteed to be true whenever the inner code executes\:

```typescript
...(huggingfaceOptions?.reasoningEffort != null && {
  reasoning: {
    effort: huggingfaceOptions.reasoningEffort,
  },
}),
```

Both versions produce identical output for all input cases \(verified via TypeScript testing against undefined\/null values\, empty objects\, empty strings\, and valid reasoning effort values\)\. Removing the redundant condition improves code clarity without changing functionality\.

</details>

```suggestion
  : GatewayModelId | keyof RegisteredProviderModels;
```

The `GlobalProviderModelId` conditional type will break access to `GatewayModelId` models when custom models are registered\. When `RegisteredProviderModels` is extended with custom model IDs\, users lose access to all gateway models and can only use the registered custom models\.


<details>
<summary>View Details</summary>
<!-- PATCH_DETAILS_PLACEHOLDER -->

### Analysis
## GlobalProviderModelId loses gateway models when custom models are registered

**What fails\:** The `GlobalProviderModelId` conditional type in `packages/ai/src/types/language-model.ts` \(line 31\-35\) resolves to `keyof RegisteredProviderModels` when custom models are registered via declaration merging\. This excludes `GatewayModelId` models entirely\, making them inaccessible\.

**How to reproduce\:**

```typescript
// Declare custom models in global scope
declare global {
  interface RegisteredProviderModels {
    'my-provider:my-model': true;
  }
}

// Try to use a gateway model - fails with current implementation
const model: GlobalProviderModelId = 'openai/gpt-4o'; 
// Type '"openai/gpt-4o"' is not assignable to type 'keyof RegisteredProviderModels'
```

**Result\:** TypeScript compilation error \- gateway models cannot be used when custom models are registered

**Expected\:** Both gateway models from `GatewayModelId` and custom registered models should be available simultaneously\, as indicated by the documentation example in the same file

**Fix applied\:** Changed the false branch of the conditional type from `keyof RegisteredProviderModels` to `GatewayModelId | keyof RegisteredProviderModels` to ensure both sets of models are available

</details>

body:
The code is reading from the wrong property name \(`'calls'` instead of `'allCalls'`\)\, which prevents proper accumulation of metadata across multiple image generation calls\.
View Details
📝 Patch Details ```diff diff --git a/packages/ai/src/generate-image/generate-image.ts b/packages/ai/src/generate-image/generate-image.ts index 34a16ea34..de823e3c5 100644 --- a/packages/ai/src/generate-image/generate-image.ts +++ b/packages/ai/src/generate-image/generate-image.ts @@ -205,7 +205,7 @@ Only applicable for HTTP-based providers. ...metadata, } as Record; const existingCalls = - (currentEntry as Record)['calls']; + (currentEntry as Record)['allCalls']; const callsArray = Array.isArray(existingCalls) ? (existingCalls as unknown[]) : []; @@ -243,6 +243,11 @@ Only applicable for HTTP-based providers. responses.push(result.response); } + // Remove internal allCalls tracking from gateway metadata before returning + if (providerMetadata['gateway'] && typeof providerMetadata['gateway'] === 'object') { + delete (providerMetadata['gateway'] as Record)['allCalls']; + } + logWarnings({ warnings, provider: model.provider, model: model.modelId }); if (!images.length) { ```
### Analysis ## Property name mismatch prevents proper metadata accumulation in multi\-call image generation **What fails\:** `generateImage()` in `packages/ai/src/generate-image/generate-image.ts` fails to properly accumulate gateway provider metadata across multiple image generation calls because it reads from the wrong property name \(`'calls'` instead of `'allCalls'`\) **How to reproduce\:** Call `generateImage()` with parameters that require multiple API calls to the gateway provider \(e\.g\.\, requesting 5 images when `maxImagesPerCall=2`\)\. This results in multiple calls to `model.doGenerate()` which each return gateway provider metadata\. **Result\:** When the code processes the second and subsequent calls\, it tries to retrieve existing accumulated calls from `['calls']` \(line 208\)\, but the property is actually named `['allCalls']` \(set on lines 217 and 213\)\. Since `undefined` is not an array\, the code creates an empty array and overwrites the previously accumulated metadata with only the new metadata\. **Expected\:** All metadata from multiple gateway provider calls should be properly accumulated\, not lost\. **Root cause\:** The \"Second pass\" commit introduced a new metadata accumulation mechanism using `allCalls`\, but\: 1. Line 208 reads from `['calls']` instead of `['allCalls']` \(property name mismatch\) 2. The `allCalls` property was being exposed in the final API result as an implementation detail **Fix\:** * Changed line 208 to read from `['allCalls']` to match the property name being written * Added cleanup code to remove the internal `allCalls` tracking property from the gateway metadata before returning the result to the caller

body:
Agreed that the whole block needs to be refactored. As a temporary solution to ship image models asap, 2 paths I see are:

1. Go with my code in an [earlier commit](https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/10478/commits/e31ac1826615266316f69400771a23c89a2f194b) that sums the cost and sets the cost field to the true total cost
2. Go with the current code in the PR that adds an `allCalls` array to the provider metadata containing the metadata for each request, and let the user sum the costs if they want. The only real issue with this is the metadata output gets quite long, and can be somewhat confusing because the data outside the `allCalls` array is just for the last request and shows the cost of one image (same issue), so if a user doesn’t read into the `allCalls` array they won’t realize what the actual cost is.

I was leaning towards option 1, but I realized that other fields other than `cost` are also being overwritten with the last request's metadata. This could be an issue as we'd only return fields like `modelAttempts`, `generationId`, `resolvedProvider`, etc for the last request if n > 1. So maybe option 2 is the best because it returns metadata from all calls. I'm just concerned about the duplicative-ness of the last call's metadata being outside `allCalls` (in the top level `providerMetadata` object) and also in the last position of the `allCalls` array.

### Analysis
## Malformed markdown code fences in Cortex Memory provider documentation

**What fails\:** Installation code blocks in the Cortex Memory provider documentation have invalid markdown syntax \- the opening code fence and command content are on the same line\, and the closing fence is on the same line as the content\.

**How to reproduce\:** View the file `content/providers/03-community-providers/69-cortex-memory.mdx` at lines 38\-39\, 42\-43\, and 46\-47\. The code blocks incorrectly use\:

**Result\:** According to [CommonMark markdown specification](https://spec.commonmark.org/0.30/#code-fence)\, the opening fence must be on its own line with optional language identifier\. The malformed syntax violates this specification and prevents proper rendering of code blocks\.

**Expected behavior\:** Installation instructions should follow the established pattern used in other community provider documentation \(31 out of 37 files\) by using `<Snippet>` components within `<Tab>` elements\, which properly displays formatted code snippets for package managers \(npm\, pnpm\, yarn\)\.

**Fix applied\:** Replaced the three malformed markdown code fence blocks with proper `<Snippet>` component syntax\, aligning with codebase patterns established in files like `02-qwen.mdx`\, `70-mem0.mdx`\, and `13-openrouter.mdx`\.

This documentation currently covers the stable v0.1.0 release. + + +### Planned Features (v0.2.0) -Enhanced streaming capabilities powered by the new `rememberStream()` API: +Enhanced streaming capabilities powered by the new `rememberStream()` API (coming soon): - **📊 Stream Metrics** - Real-time monitoring of latency, throughput, tokens, and costs - **🔄 Progressive Storage** - Store partial responses during streaming for resumability @@ -37,7 +41,7 @@ Enhanced streaming capabilities powered by the new `rememberStream()` API: - **🧬 Progressive Fact Extraction** - Extract facts incrementally during streaming - **🔁 Error Recovery** - Handle interrupted streams with resume tokens -All features are opt-in and fully backward compatible. +All features will be opt-in and fully backward compatible. ## Setup ```
### Analysis ## Documentation describes v0\.2\.0 features for v0\.1\.0 package **What fails\:** The Cortex Memory documentation includes a \"What\'s New in v0\.2\.0\" section describing streaming capabilities \(`rememberStream()` API\, streaming hooks\, progressive fact extraction\) while the documented installation specifies `@cortexmemory/vercel-ai-provider`\: \^0\.1\.0\, which does not include these features\. **How to reproduce\:** 1. Follow the installation instructions at lines 42\-59 2. Install `@cortexmemory/vercel-ai-provider` version 0\.1\.0 as documented 3. Attempt to use features described in lines 30\-40 \(rememberStream\, onChunk\, onProgress callbacks\, etc\.\) **Result\:** The installed package \(v0\.1\.0\) does not support the documented v0\.2\.0 features\, resulting in API not found errors if users try to implement the features described as new in v0\.2\.0\. **Expected\:** The documentation should clearly indicate which features are planned for future releases versus available in the current v0\.1\.0 release\. Without this distinction\, users installing the documented version will encounter features that don\'t exist\, causing confusion and implementation failures\. **Fix\:** Moved the v0\.2\.0 features section to a \"Planned Features \(v0\.2\.0\)\" subsection with a warning note indicating these features are not yet available in v0\.1\.0\.

### Analysis ## Build failure: Streamdown dependency incompatibility with ESM module resolution **What fails:** Build of `@example/next-openai-pages` fails during Next.js page data collection when using `streamdown@1.6.3`. **How to reproduce:** ```bash pnpm turbo run build --filter="@example/next-openai-pages" ``` **Error message:** ``` Error: Cannot find module '/path/to/node_modules/.pnpm/streamdown@1.6.3_.../@types+mdast@4.0.4.../streamdown/dist/chunk-JZKDZQ6K.js' imported from '...lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/check' Did you mean to import "lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/check.js"? ``` **Root cause:** The `streamdown@1.6.3` package was recently added as a dependency to the `@example/next-openai-pages` example application. However, this version has a transitive dependency on `lucide-react@0.542.0` that contains ESM imports without `.js` file extensions, causing module resolution failures in strict ESM contexts (such as Next.js 15's module resolution). **Solution:** Removed the `streamdown` dependency and reverted the related code changes in `@example/next-openai-pages` back to using standard `
` elements for text rendering instead of the `` component. The build now succeeds without errors. **Files modified:** - `examples/next-openai-pages/package.json` - Removed streamdown dependency - `examples/next-openai-pages/pages/chat/generate-chat/index.tsx` - Removed import and replaced Streamdown component with div - `examples/next-openai-pages/pages/tools/call-tool/index.tsx` - Removed import and replaced Streamdown component with div - `pnpm-lock.yaml` - Updated lockfile after dependency removal

### Analysis

## ESM Module Resolution Error: Missing .js extensions in streamdown build output

**What fails:** The `@example/next-openai-pages` build fails during Next.js page collection phase. The `streamdown@1.6.3` package's bundled code imports from `lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/{icon-name}` without the required `.js` file extension, which breaks ESM module resolution in Node.js strict mode.

**How to reproduce:**
```bash
pnpm install
pnpm turbo run build --filter=@example/next-openai-pages
```

**Result:**
```
[Error: Cannot find module '/path/to/node_modules/.pnpm/streamdown@1.6.3_.../lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/check' 
imported from streamdown/dist/chunk-JZKDZQ6K.js
Did you mean to import "lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/check.js"?]
```

**Root cause:** The `streamdown@1.6.3` package's bundled JavaScript output contains bare ESM imports to lucide-react icon files without `.js` extensions. Modern Node.js (v22+) and strict ESM mode require explicit file extensions for all module imports. This is a breaking change in Node.js module resolution that affects libraries with bundled code that hasn't been updated.

**Fix applied:** Created a pnpm patch (`patches/streamdown@1.6.3.patch`) that adds `.js` extensions to all nine lucide-react icon imports in the bundled output file (`dist/chunk-JZKDZQ6K.js`):
- `lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/check` → `lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/check.js`
- `lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/copy` → `lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/copy.js`
- `lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/download` → `lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/download.js`
- `lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/loader-2` → `lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/loader-2.js`
- `lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/maximize-2` → `lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/maximize-2.js`
- `lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/rotate-ccw` → `lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/rotate-ccw.js`
- `lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/x` → `lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/x.js`
- `lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/zoom-in` → `lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/zoom-in.js`
- `lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/zoom-out` → `lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/zoom-out.js`

**Verification:** The build now completes successfully, generating all 19 static pages without errors.

## Streamdown version inconsistency in next\-fastapi example

**What fails\:** The `next-fastapi` example specifies `streamdown@^1.6.3` while all other examples \(`next-agent`\, `next-openai`\, `next-openai-pages`\, `next`\) specify `streamdown@^1.6.4`\. This causes the next\-fastapi example to miss the lucide imports fix included in version 1\.6\.4\.

**How to reproduce\:**

1.  Check `examples/next-fastapi/package.json` \- shows `streamdown@^1.6.3` on line 20
2.  Compare with `examples/next-agent/package.json`\, `examples/next-openai/package.json`\, etc\. \- all show `streamdown@^1.6.4`
3.  Verify via git history\: commit f1b843476 \(\"Bump Streamdown\"\) updated 4 examples but missed next\-fastapi

**Result\:** The next\-fastapi example uses an outdated version that lacks the \"Restore original lucide imports\" fix from version 1\.6\.4\, while all other examples have the corrected version\. This inconsistency means developers comparing examples see different dependency versions\.

**Expected\:** All examples should use the same tested version of streamdown for consistency\. According to [Streamdown\'s GitHub releases](https://github.com/vercel/streamdown/releases)\, version 1\.6\.4 is the current patch that fixes lucide imports \(published November 23\)\. All examples should specify `streamdown@^1.6.4`\.

### Analysis

## Outdated pnpm-lock.yaml causes frozen-lockfile installation failure

**What fails:** The `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` command fails because pnpm-lock.yaml is out of sync with package.json files after the Streamdown version bump.

**How to reproduce:**
```bash
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
```

**Result:**
```
[ERROR]  ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE  Cannot install with "frozen-lockfile" because pnpm-lock.yaml is not up to date with <ROOT>/examples/next/package.json

specifiers in the lockfile: {"streamdown":"^1.6.4",...} don't match specs in package.json: {"streamdown":"^1.6.5",...}
```

**Root cause:** Commit `b24edf71c` ("Bump Streamdown") updated the package.json files in multiple example projects to streamdown@^1.6.5 but did not update the pnpm-lock.yaml file, which still contained streamdown@^1.6.4 entries. The CI environment uses `--frozen-lockfile` by default, which requires the lockfile and package.json files to be in sync.

**Fix:** Updated pnpm-lock.yaml to reflect streamdown@^1.6.5 across all affected packages (examples/next, examples/next-agent, examples/next-fastapi, examples/next-openai, examples/next-openai-pages).

body:
In `generateObject` with `onStepFinish` continuation and multiple retry attempts\, continuation feedback messages from earlier attempts are discarded instead of accumulating\. This causes the model to only receive the latest feedback message\, losing context from previous failed attempts\.
View Details
📝 Patch Details ```diff diff --git a/packages/ai/src/generate-object/generate-object.ts b/packages/ai/src/generate-object/generate-object.ts index 53de2c6b6..eb3ed5d6e 100644 --- a/packages/ai/src/generate-object/generate-object.ts +++ b/packages/ai/src/generate-object/generate-object.ts @@ -335,7 +335,7 @@ functionality that can be fully encapsulated in the provider. const initialMessages = standardizedPrompt.messages; let currentMessages: Array = [...initialMessages]; - let nextStepContinuationMessages: Array = []; + let accumulatedContinuationMessages: Array = []; let result: string; let finishReason: FinishReason; @@ -353,12 +353,11 @@ functionality that can be fully encapsulated in the provider. do { attemptCount++; - // Combine initial messages with continuation messages + // Combine initial messages with accumulated continuation messages const stepInputMessages = [ ...currentMessages, - ...nextStepContinuationMessages, + ...accumulatedContinuationMessages, ]; - nextStepContinuationMessages = []; // Clear after use const promptMessages = await convertToLanguageModelPrompt({ prompt: { @@ -530,8 +529,10 @@ functionality that can be fully encapsulated in the provider. 'continue' in onStepFinishResult ) { if (onStepFinishResult.continue === true) { - // Store continuation messages for the next step's input - nextStepContinuationMessages = onStepFinishResult.messages; + // Accumulate continuation messages for the next step's input + accumulatedContinuationMessages.push( + ...onStepFinishResult.messages, + ); shouldContinue = true; } // continue: false means stop ```
### Analysis ## Continuation feedback messages discarded on retry attempts in `generateObject` **What fails\:** In `generateObject` with `onStepFinish` continuation and multiple retry attempts \(maxRetries \> 0\)\, continuation feedback messages from earlier failed attempts are discarded instead of accumulated\. The model receives only the latest feedback message\, losing context from previous validation failures\. **How to reproduce\:** When using `generateObject` with\: * A schema that fails validation on the first attempt * An `onStepFinish` callback that returns `continue: true` with feedback messages * Multiple retry attempts before success The expected behavior is\: ``` Attempt 1: [initial_prompt] → invalid Attempt 2: [initial_prompt + feedback_1] → invalid Attempt 3: [initial_prompt + feedback_1 + feedback_2] → success ``` **Actual behavior \(before fix\)\:** ``` Attempt 1: [initial_prompt] → invalid Attempt 2: [initial_prompt + feedback_1] → invalid Attempt 3: [initial_prompt + feedback_2] ← feedback_1 is LOST ``` **Root cause\:** In `packages/ai/src/generate-object/generate-object.ts` lines 338 and 534\: * Line 338\: `nextStepContinuationMessages` initialized as empty array * Line 363 \(old\)\: `nextStepContinuationMessages = []` clears after each use * Line 534 \(old\)\: `nextStepContinuationMessages = onStepFinishResult.messages` replaces instead of accumulating This caused messages to be replaced rather than accumulated across iterations\, losing earlier feedback\. **The fix\:** Changed the logic to accumulate continuation messages across attempts\: * Renamed `nextStepContinuationMessages` to `accumulatedContinuationMessages` for clarity * Removed the line that cleared messages after use * Changed line 534 from assignment to `push()` to accumulate messages\: `accumulatedContinuationMessages.push(...onStepFinishResult.messages)` This ensures the model receives full context from all previous validation failures\, matching the pattern used in `generateText` with `responseMessages` accumulation and aligning with the documented behavior that \"messages injected via continuation are added to message history\.\"

body:
Hmm I see this a legit problem but it's probably best to give the developer control over the message history. The ideal solution would allow for accumulation, no accumulation, or direct control over the message history.

This highlights something else. Is it desirable to have a message history that preserves the validation errors? Illustration below: 

## Options
### Current Behavior:
```markdown
Message History: 
- UserMessage: ...
- AssistantMessage: <--validation success
```

### Detailed History With Messages
```markdown
Message History: 
- UserMessage ...
- AssistantMessage <--validation failed 
- UserMessage: "You failed bc of XYZ. Regenerate." <-- validation failure feedback
- AssistantMessage: <--validation success
```

### Detailed History With Tool Injection
```markdown
Detailed Message History With Inserted Tool: 
- UserMessage ...
- ToolMessage <-- validation failure feedback with original message
- AssistantMessage: <--validation success
```

---

Of these choices, it's probably best to consider a tool injection so that we can preserve everything! However, I'm biased to my use cases where I'm attempting to be token efficient and support models without tool calling prowess.

Making the `candidates` field optional breaks the type definitions that depend on it\. The types at lines 893\, 896\, 904\, and 908 attempt to access array elements via `['candidates'][number]`\, which is invalid when `candidates` is optional \(could be `undefined`\)\.
View Details
📝 Patch Details ```diff diff --git a/packages/google/src/google-generative-ai-language-model.ts b/packages/google/src/google-generative-ai-language-model.ts index 7c6557f5b..c8b6f11d9 100644 --- a/packages/google/src/google-generative-ai-language-model.ts +++ b/packages/google/src/google-generative-ai-language-model.ts @@ -890,10 +890,10 @@ const responseSchema = lazySchema(() => ); type ContentSchema = NonNullable< - InferSchema['candidates'][number]['content'] + NonNullable['candidates']>[number]['content'] >; export type GroundingMetadataSchema = NonNullable< - InferSchema['candidates'][number]['groundingMetadata'] + NonNullable['candidates']>[number]['groundingMetadata'] >; type GroundingChunkSchema = NonNullable< @@ -901,11 +901,11 @@ type GroundingChunkSchema = NonNullable< >[number]; export type UrlContextMetadataSchema = NonNullable< - InferSchema['candidates'][number]['urlContextMetadata'] + NonNullable['candidates']>[number]['urlContextMetadata'] >; export type SafetyRatingSchema = NonNullable< - InferSchema['candidates'][number]['safetyRatings'] + NonNullable['candidates']>[number]['safetyRatings'] >[number]; // limited version of the schema, focussed on what is needed for the implementation ```
### Analysis ## Optional `candidates` field breaks type definitions in responseSchema **What fails\:** TypeScript compilation fails with TS2537 errors when `candidates` field is marked as optional with `.optional()` at line 880\, because type definitions at lines 893\, 896\, 904\, and 908 attempt to index into the optional field using `['candidates'][number]`\, which is invalid when the field can be `undefined`\. **How to reproduce\:** ```bash cd packages/google pnpm type-check ``` **Result\:** TypeScript compiler throws four TS2537 errors\: * `src/google-generative-ai-language-model.ts(893,52): error TS2537: Type '...' has no matching index signature for type 'number'.` * `src/google-generative-ai-language-model.ts(896,52): error TS2537: Type '...' has no matching index signature for type 'number'.` * `src/google-generative-ai-language-model.ts(904,52): error TS2537: Type '...' has no matching index signature for type 'number'.` * `src/google-generative-ai-language-model.ts(908,52): error TS2537: Type '...' has no matching index signature for type 'number'.` **Expected\:** TypeScript compilation should succeed\. The type definitions need to wrap the optional `candidates` field with `NonNullable` before attempting to index it\, narrowing the type from `Array | undefined` to `Array`\. **Fix\:** Wrap `InferSchema['candidates']` with `NonNullable` in all four type definitions \(ContentSchema\, GroundingMetadataSchema\, UrlContextMetadataSchema\, and SafetyRatingSchema\)\.

**Additional Suggestion:** The code will crash at runtime if the `candidates` field is `undefined` or `null`\, since it directly accesses `response.candidates[0]` without checking if `candidates` exists first\.
View Details
📝 Patch Details ```diff diff --git a/packages/google/src/google-generative-ai-language-model.ts b/packages/google/src/google-generative-ai-language-model.ts index e02f8a4d8..8c8e004b6 100644 --- a/packages/google/src/google-generative-ai-language-model.ts +++ b/packages/google/src/google-generative-ai-language-model.ts @@ -210,7 +210,16 @@ export class GoogleGenerativeAILanguageModel implements LanguageModelV3 { fetch: this.config.fetch, }); - const candidate = response.candidates[0]; + const candidate = response.candidates?.[0]; + + if (candidate == null) { + throw new Error( + 'No candidates returned from Google Generative AI API. ' + + 'This can happen when the prompt is blocked by safety filters. ' + + `Check promptFeedback for details: ${JSON.stringify(response.promptFeedback)}` + ); + } + const content: Array = []; // map ordered parts to content: ```
### Analysis ## Unsafe access to candidates array in GoogleGenerativeAILanguageModel\.doGenerate\(\) **What fails\:** `doGenerate()` method in `packages/google/src/google-generative-ai-language-model.ts` crashes at runtime when the Google Generative AI API returns a response with `candidates` field set to `null` or `undefined`\. **How to reproduce\:** The schema at line 894 defines `candidates: z.array(...).nullish()`\, which allows the field to be `null`\, `undefined`\, or missing\. When the API returns such a response \(which can happen when the prompt is blocked by safety filters\)\, the code at line 213 attempts to access `response.candidates[0]` without checking if `candidates` exists first\. Example that triggers the error\: ```typescript // API returns: { candidates: null, promptFeedback: {...} } const candidate = response.candidates[0]; // TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading '0') ``` **Result\:** Runtime error \- `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading '0')` or similar **Expected\:** Should handle missing\/null candidates gracefully with a descriptive error\, consistent with how `doStream()` handles this at line 400 using optional chaining `value.candidates?.[0]` **Related code pattern\:** The `doStream()` method correctly handles this case\: ```typescript const candidate = value.candidates?.[0]; if (candidate == null) { return; } ``` **API Reference\:** [Google Gemini API documentation](https://ai.google.dev/api/generate-content) indicates `candidates` field is optional and can be missing when the prompt is blocked or fails content filtering\. **Fix applied\:** Added optional chaining and null check before accessing candidates array\, with a descriptive error message for debugging\.

**What fails\:** The Tavily code example in `content/cookbook/05-node/56-web-search-agent.mdx` \(line 183\) imports only `tavilySearch` but uses `tavilyExtract()` on line 191\, causing a `ReferenceError: tavilyExtract is not defined` at runtime

```ts
import { generateText, stepCountIs } from 'ai';
import { tavilySearch } from '@tavily/ai-sdk';  // ← Missing tavilyExtract
import { openai } from '@ai-sdk/openai';

    webExtract: tavilyExtract()  // ← ReferenceError: tavilyExtract is not defined
```

**Expected behavior\:** According to the [official Tavily AI SDK documentation](https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/integrations/vercel)\, `tavilyExtract` is a valid export from `@tavily/ai-sdk` and must be imported separately\. The import statement should include both functions as shown in the Parallel Web example \(line 215\) which correctly imports both `searchTool` and `extractTool`


The path traversal check using `startsWith` is insufficient and allows escaping the workspace directory by crafting paths with similar names \(e\.g\.\, `/workspace_evil` can escape `/workspace`\)\.


<details>
<summary>View Details</summary>
<!-- PATCH_DETAILS_PLACEHOLDER -->

### Analysis
## Path Traversal Vulnerability in WorkspaceEditor\.resolve\(\)

**What fails\:** The `WorkspaceEditor.resolve()` method in `examples/next-openai/lib/apply-patch-file-editor.ts` uses insufficient path validation allowing directory escape via crafted paths with similar directory names \(e\.g\.\, `/workspace_evil` escapes `/workspace`\)\.

**How to reproduce\:**

```typescript
const editor = new WorkspaceEditor('/workspace');
const result = await editor.resolve('../workspace_evil/secret.txt');
// Returns: /workspace_evil/secret.txt (SHOULD HAVE THROWN ERROR)
```

The vulnerability exists because `startsWith()` check matches string prefixes without validating path separators\:

*   Resolves to `/workspace_evil/secret.txt`
*   Check\: `/workspace_evil/secret.txt`\.startsWith\(`/workspace`\) returns `true` ✓
*   Path is OUTSIDE workspace but check passes due to similar prefix

**Result\:** Attacker can read\/write files outside workspace directory by using paths like `../workspace_evil/`\, `../workspace2/`\, etc\.

**Expected\:** Should throw `Error: Operation outside workspace` for any paths attempting to escape the workspace root directory\.

**Fix implemented\:** Changed validation from simple `startsWith()` check to proper path normalization using `path.relative()`\:

*   Before\: `if (!resolved.startsWith(this.root))`
*   After\: `const relative = path.relative(this.root, resolved); if (relative.startsWith('..') || path.isAbsolute(relative))`

This correctly identifies and blocks all escape attempts while preserving legitimate file operations\.

</details>
<!-- VADE-CATEGORY: security -->

The `apply_patch_call` streaming handler emits a tool\-call in both the `.added` event \(line 1040\) and the `.done` event \(line 1247\) when status is \'completed\'\, which would cause duplicate tool\-call emissions if the API returns `.added` with `status: 'completed'`\.


<details>

<!-- PATCH_DETAILS_PLACEHOLDER -->

### Analysis
## Duplicate tool\-call emissions for apply\_patch\_call when status is \'completed\' in \.added event

**What fails\:** The `OpenAIResponsesLanguageModel.doStream()` method can emit duplicate `tool-call` events for the same `apply_patch_call` item if the OpenAI Responses API sends a `.added` event with `status: 'completed'` followed by a `.done` event\, also with `status: 'completed'`\.

**How to reproduce\:**  
The streaming handler has conditional tool\-call emissions in both the `response.output_item.added` event handler \(line 1031\-1054\) and the `response.output_item.done` event handler \(line 1242\-1261\)\. Both check `if (value.item.status === 'completed')` before emitting identical tool\-call events with the same `toolCallId`\.

While current test fixtures show `.added` events with `status: 'in_progress'` and `.done` events with `status: 'completed'`\, the API schema allows both events to carry either status value\. If the API sends `.added` with `status: 'completed'`\, both handlers would emit the tool\-call\, resulting in two identical events with the same `toolCallId`\.

**What happens vs expected\:**

*   **Current behavior with hypothetical API change\:** If `.added` comes with `status: 'completed'`\, then `.done` also with `status: 'completed'` → two `tool-call` events emitted with identical `toolCallId` and operation data
*   **Expected behavior\:** Only one `tool-call` event should be emitted per `apply_patch_call` item

The fix removes the conditional emission from the `.added` handler \(where the item is added but potentially incomplete\) and keeps the emission only in the `.done` handler \(where the operation is finalized\)\. This ensures a single emission regardless of status values in the `.added` event\.

</details>

The validation logic checks for a `'type'` property that doesn\'t exist on `SystemModelMessage`\. It should check for the `'role'` property instead\, which is the actual distinguishing field in the object\.


<details>
<summary>View Details</summary>
<!-- PATCH_DETAILS_PLACEHOLDER -->

### Analysis
## Incorrect property check in standardizePrompt validation

**What fails\:** `standardizePrompt()` checks for a non\-existent `'type'` property instead of the actual `'role'` property when validating system messages\. This causes the validation to either pass for invalid reasons or miss detecting invalid objects\.

**How to reproduce\:** The validation in lines 41\-46 of `packages/ai/src/prompt/standardize-prompt.ts` checks\:

```typescript
if (
  prompt.system != null &&
  typeof prompt.system !== 'string' &&
  'type' in prompt.system &&
  prompt.system.type !== 'system'
)
```

However\, `SystemModelMessage` \(defined in `packages/provider-utils/src/types/system-model-message.ts`\) has the structure `{ role: 'system'; content: string; ... }`\, not a `type` property\.

**Result\:**

*   Valid `SystemModelMessage` objects with `role: 'system'` pass validation for the wrong reason \(because `'type'` doesn\'t exist in them\)
*   Invalid objects like `{}` or `{ content: 'test' }` also pass validation because they lack the `'type'` property
*   These invalid objects reach `convertToLanguageModelPrompt()` where accessing `prompt.system.content` creates system messages with `undefined` content and provider options

**Expected behavior\:** The validation should check for the `'role'` property \(the actual field in `SystemModelMessage`\)\, ensuring that only objects with `role: 'system'` pass when an object is provided\.

**Fix applied\:** Changed the validation to check `'role' in prompt.system && prompt.system.role !== 'system'` instead of checking for `'type'`\.

</details>

## Non\-existent method call in next\-basic\-chat example

**What fails\:** The chat route in `examples/next-basic-chat/app/api/chat/route.ts` calls `result.toDataStreamResponse()`\, which does not exist on the `StreamTextResult` object\.

*   **Expected\:** Should return a properly formatted response compatible with the `useChat` hook

All 30\+ other examples in the codebase use `toUIMessageStreamResponse()`\, and a [codemod exists](https://vercel.com/packages/codemod/src/codemods/v5/rename-todatastreamresponse-to-touimessagestreamresponse.ts) that automatically migrates from the old `toDataStreamResponse` API to `toUIMessageStreamResponse`\.

```suggestion
    Object.entries(tools).find(([_, tool]) => tool?.name === toolName)?.[1] ??
```

The `getTool` function returns a tuple `[key, tool]` instead of just the tool when finding by name property\, causing tool execution to fail at runtime\.


<details>
<summary>View Details</summary>
<!-- PATCH_DETAILS_PLACEHOLDER -->

### Analysis
## getTool function returns tuple instead of tool when finding by name property

**What fails\:** When `getTool()` searches for a tool by its `name` property\, `Object.entries().find()` returns the entire `[key, tool]` tuple instead of extracting the tool object\. This causes tool execution to fail at runtime in `execute-tool-call.ts` line 37 and `stream-text.ts` line 1485\, where accessing `tool?.execute` and `tool?.onInputDelta` returns `undefined` on the tuple\.

**How to reproduce\:**

```typescript
const tools = {
  weatherTool: tool({ name: 'weather', inputSchema: z.object({}) }),
};

const foundTool = getTool('weather', tools); // Finding by name property
if (foundTool?.execute == null) {
  // Execution path: This condition is TRUE even though the tool exists
  // because foundTool is ['weatherTool', toolObject] (array)
  // and arrays don't have .execute property
  return undefined; // Tool not executed
}
```

**Result\:** Tools found by name property silently fail to execute\. The check `if (tool?.execute == null)` always evaluates to true when tools are found by name\, causing the tool invocation to be skipped\.

**Expected\:** `getTool()` should always return a `Tool | undefined`\, never a tuple\. When a tool is found by name via `Object.entries().find()`\, the function must extract the second element of the returned `[key, tool]` tuple\.

**Fix\:** Add optional chaining to extract the tool from the tuple\: `Object.entries(tools).find(...)?.[1]` instead of `Object.entries(tools).find(...)`

</details>

body:
```suggestion
              if (usage.inputTokens === undefined) {
```

The condition `if (!usage.inputTokens)` uses truthiness check which incorrectly treats a valid value of `0` tokens as \"not set\"\, causing it to overwrite correct values from `message_start` with fallback values from `message_delta`\.


<details>
<summary>View Details</summary>
<!-- PATCH_DETAILS_PLACEHOLDER -->

### Analysis
## Falsy check on `usage.inputTokens` causes overwriting valid zero value

**What fails\:** In `anthropic-messages-language-model.ts:1488`\, the condition `if (!usage.inputTokens)` uses a truthiness check that incorrectly treats `input_tokens: 0` \(a valid Anthropic API value\) as \"not set\"\, causing it to overwrite the correct zero value with a fallback value from `message_delta`\.

**How to reproduce\:**

1.  Call the Anthropic Messages API with a prompt that results in `message_start` event containing `usage.input_tokens: 0` \(e\.g\.\, when using cache hits or other edge cases\)
2.  The stream handler receives the `message_start` event and sets `usage.inputTokens = 0`
3.  When `message_delta` arrives with `usage: { output_tokens: X, input_tokens: Y, ... }`\, the falsy check on line 1488 evaluates to `true` \(since `0 && true` is falsy in JavaScript\)
4.  The code executes `usage.inputTokens = value.usage.input_tokens ?? 0`\, overwriting the correct `0` with the `message_delta` value

**Result\:** The final reported `inputTokens` is incorrect \- it uses the value from `message_delta` instead of the value from `message_start`

**Expected\:** According to [Anthropic API documentation](https://docs.claude.com/en/api/messages)\, `input_tokens` has a minimum value of 0\, meaning zero is a valid and legitimate value\. The fallback should only trigger when `inputTokens` hasn\'t been set \(is `undefined`\)\, not when it\'s legitimately set to `0`\.

**Fix\:** Change the condition from `if (!usage.inputTokens)` to `if (usage.inputTokens === undefined)` to explicitly check for undefined rather than relying on truthiness\. This properly distinguishes between \"not set\" \(undefined\) and \"set to zero\" \(0\)\.

</details>

### Analysis
## Incorrect deferLoading example in toolSearch\_20251119 JSDoc

**What fails\:** The JSDoc example in `toolSearch_20251119()` shows using `providerOptions.anthropic.deferLoading` to defer tool loading\, but this property is never read by the implementation\. Tools that follow this example will not have their definitions deferred\.

**How to reproduce\:** Following the example in the JSDoc comment\:

```typescript
tool({
  description: 'Create a pull request',
  inputSchema: z.object({ ... }),
  providerOptions: {
    anthropic: { deferLoading: true }
```

**Expected\:** The `experimental_deferLoading` property should be used at the tool level instead\, as documented in [ADVANCED\_TOOL\_USE\.md](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/packages/anthropic/ADVANCED_TOOL_USE.md#usage) \(lines 69\, 82\, 380\)\:

```typescript
tool({
  description: 'Create a pull request',
  inputSchema: z.object({ ... }),
  experimental_deferLoading: true,
})
```

**Root cause\:** The implementation in `packages/ai/src/prompt/prepare-tools-and-tool-choice.ts` \(line 57\) reads from `tool.experimental_deferLoading`\, not from `providerOptions`\. The JSDoc example in `packages/anthropic/src/tool/tool-search_20251119.ts` \(lines 77\-79\) incorrectly demonstrated the former pattern\.

The code attempts to extract `size`\, `quality`\, `background`\, and `output_format` from the API response\, but the OpenAI Images API does not return these fields\. This causes all images to have these metadata fields set to `undefined`\, defeating the stated purpose of extracting metadata for cost computation\.
View Details
📝 Patch Details ```diff diff --git a/packages/openai/src/image/openai-image-model.test.ts b/packages/openai/src/image/openai-image-model.test.ts index e35424588..99ddbb43c 100644 --- a/packages/openai/src/image/openai-image-model.test.ts +++ b/packages/openai/src/image/openai-image-model.test.ts @@ -269,9 +269,8 @@ describe('doGenerate', () => { images: [ { created: 1733837122, - size: undefined, + size: '1024x1024', quality: undefined, - background: undefined, outputFormat: undefined, }, ], @@ -315,17 +314,15 @@ describe('doGenerate', () => { revisedPrompt: 'A charming visual illustration of a baby sea otter swimming joyously.', created: 1733837122, - size: undefined, + size: '1024x1024', quality: undefined, - background: undefined, - outputFormat: undefined, + outputFormat: 'b64_json', }, { created: 1733837122, - size: undefined, + size: '1024x1024', quality: undefined, - background: undefined, - outputFormat: undefined, + outputFormat: 'b64_json', }, ], }, diff --git a/packages/openai/src/image/openai-image-model.ts b/packages/openai/src/image/openai-image-model.ts index ccb3c0aa1..9dd685ace 100644 --- a/packages/openai/src/image/openai-image-model.ts +++ b/packages/openai/src/image/openai-image-model.ts @@ -63,6 +63,13 @@ export class OpenAIImageModel implements ImageModelV3 { } const currentDate = this.config._internal?.currentDate?.() ?? new Date(); + + // Capture the requested parameters for metadata + const requestedQuality = (providerOptions.openai?.quality as string) ?? undefined; + const requestedSize = size ?? undefined; + const responseFormat = (providerOptions.openai?.response_format as string) ?? + (!hasDefaultResponseFormat.has(this.modelId) ? 'b64_json' : undefined); + const { value: response, responseHeaders } = await postJsonToApi({ url: this.config.url({ path: '/images/generations', @@ -110,10 +117,9 @@ export class OpenAIImageModel implements ImageModelV3 { ? { revisedPrompt: item.revised_prompt } : {}), created: response.created ?? undefined, - size: response.size ?? undefined, - quality: response.quality ?? undefined, - background: response.background ?? undefined, - outputFormat: response.output_format ?? undefined, + size: requestedSize, + quality: requestedQuality, + outputFormat: responseFormat, })), }, }, ```
### Analysis ## OpenAI Images API metadata fields always undefined **What fails\:** Image metadata fields \(`size`\, `quality`\, `outputFormat`\) are always undefined in `providerMetadata.openai.images` for generated images\, making the metadata unusable for cost computation\. **How to reproduce\:** ```typescript const image = await generateImage({ model: 'dall-e-3', prompt: 'A sea otter', size: '1024x1024', providerOptions: { openai: { quality: 'hd' } } }); console.log(image.providerMetadata?.openai?.images?.[0]); // Was: { created: 1733837122, size: undefined, quality: undefined, ... } // Now: { created: 1733837122, size: '1024x1024', quality: 'hd', ... } ``` **Root cause\:** The code attempted to extract `size`\, `quality`\, `background`\, and `output_format` from the OpenAI API response \(lines 112\-116 of openai\-image\-model\.ts\)\, but per [OpenAI\'s documentation](https://cookbook.openai.com/examples/dalle/image_generations_edits_and_variations_with_dall-e)\, these fields are NOT returned in the API response\. The response only contains `created`\, `data` array\, and `usage` fields\. **Fix\:** Capture the requested parameters from the input before the API call instead of trying to extract them from the response\: * `size`\: From the `size` input parameter * `quality`\: From `providerOptions.openai.quality` * `outputFormat`\: From `providerOptions.openai.response_format` or the default \'b64\_json\' * Removed `background` field as it doesn\'t apply to Images API **Result\:** Metadata now accurately reflects what was requested\, enabling proper cost computation for billing purposes\.

The promise is being resolved immediately at line 1558\, before the stream\'s transform function has a chance to reject it for error responses\. This breaks error handling for HTTP 200 responses with error payloads\, as the rejection attempt at line 966 will have no effect on an already\-resolved promise\.


<details>
<summary>View Details</summary>
<!-- PATCH_DETAILS_PLACEHOLDER -->

### Analysis
## Promise pre\-resolution prevents error handling in HTTP 200 stream responses

**What fails\:** AnthropicMessagesLanguageModel\.doStream\(\) fails to propagate errors when the Anthropic API returns HTTP 200 with error payload \(e\.g\.\, overloaded\_error\)\. The error rejection in the transform function has no effect on an already\-resolved promise\.

**How to reproduce\:** The bug occurs when streaming a request and the API returns HTTP 200 with an error chunk as the first response \(as documented in the code comment\: \"The Anthropic API returns 200 responses when there are overloaded errors\"\)\:

```typescript
// At line 1558-1562, the promise is resolved immediately:
returnPromise.resolve({
  stream,
  request: { body },
  response: { headers: responseHeaders },
});

// Later, when the stream is consumed and transform() processes the first chunk,
// if it's an error (line 966):
if (chunk.value.type === 'error') {
  returnPromise.reject(new APICallError(...)); // This has no effect!
}
```

**Result\:** The promise is already settled \(resolved\) before the transform function runs\, so the rejection attempt at line 966 is ignored\. The caller receives a successful stream object instead of an error\.

**Expected\:** The error should propagate to the caller as a rejected promise\, matching the documented behavior for overloaded\_error responses \(HTTP 529 status equivalent\)\.

**Root cause\:** JavaScript Promises can only be settled once\. Once `resolve()` is called\, subsequent `reject()` calls have no effect\. The DelayedPromise wrapper in the code respects this fundamental Promise behavior \- after the promise is created and resolved\, calling `reject()` simply updates the internal status but cannot affect the already\-resolved Promise\.

**Fix\:** Remove the premature promise resolution at lines 1558\-1562\. The existing transform function logic \(lines 964\-991\) and flush function \(lines 941\-949\) properly handle all settlement cases\:

*   Error case\: `returnPromise.reject()` if first chunk is error
*   Success case\: `returnPromise.resolve()` if first chunk is valid
*   Completion case\: `returnPromise.resolve()` in flush if stream ends normally

This matches the existing test case at anthropic\-messages\-language\-model\.test\.ts\:4919 which expects error propagation for overloaded\_error responses\.

</details>

### Analysis ## Missing `strict` property passthrough in Anthropic tool preparation **What fails\:** The `prepareTools()` function in `packages/anthropic/src/anthropic-prepare-tools.ts` does not pass through the `strict` property from function tools to the Anthropic tool definition\, breaking structured output feature when `strict` is set\. **How to reproduce\:** ```bash cd packages/anthropic pnpm test:node -- src/anthropic-prepare-tools.test.ts ``` The test \"should include strict when supportsStructuredOutput is true and strict is true\" would fail with\: ``` - Expected: "strict": true + Received: (property missing) ``` **What was happening\:** When refactoring to use `getAnthropicAdvancedToolUseFeaturesSupport()`\, the handling of the `strict` property was removed\. The React peerDependency should match the version constraints in packages\/rsc to prevent users from installing incompatible React versions\.


<details>
<summary>View Details</summary>
<!-- PATCH_DETAILS_PLACEHOLDER -->

### Analysis
## Inconsistent React peer dependency constraints allows installation of vulnerable versions

**What fails\:** packages\/react declares peerDependency `"react": "^18 || ^19"` while packages\/rsc declares `"react": "^18 || ~19.0.1 || ~19.1.2 || ^19.2.1"`\. This allows npm\/yarn\/pnpm to resolve to React 19\.0\.0\, 19\.1\.0\, 19\.1\.1\, or 19\.2\.0 when packages\/react is installed\, despite packages\/rsc explicitly excluding these versions due to CVE\-2025\-55182\.

**How to reproduce\:**

```bash
# When a project depends on both @ai-sdk/react and @ai-sdk/rsc:
npm install @ai-sdk/react@3.0.0-beta.130 @ai-sdk/rsc@2.0.0-beta.131
# Without the fix, npm could resolve to React 19.0.0 or other vulnerable versions
# satisfying packages/react's constraint while violating packages/rsc's constraint
```

**Result\:** Dependency resolution allows vulnerable React versions \(19\.0\.0\, 19\.1\.0\, 19\.1\.1\, 19\.2\.0\) to satisfy the packages\/react peer dependency\, creating an inconsistent state with packages\/rsc\. Users implementing React Server Components would be exposed to CVE\-2025\-55182 \(CVSS 10\.0 critical security vulnerability\)\.

**Expected\:** Both packages should declare identical peer dependency constraints to ensure consistent security requirements\. packages\/react should exclude vulnerable versions just as packages\/rsc does\.

**Fix applied\:** Updated packages\/react\/package\.json peerDependencies from `"react": "^18 || ^19"` to `"react": "^18 || ~19.0.1 || ~19.1.2 || ^19.2.1"` to match packages\/rsc\'s constraint and exclude vulnerable React versions affected by [CVE\-2025\-55182](https://react.dev/blog/2025/12/03/critical-security-vulnerability-in-react-server-components)\.

**Security advisory\:** React 19\.0\.0\, 19\.1\.0\, 19\.1\.1\, and 19\.2\.0 contain critical vulnerabilities in React Server Components \(CVSS 10\.0\)\. These versions should be upgraded to 19\.0\.1\+\, 19\.1\.2\+\, or 19\.2\.1\+ respectively\.

</details>

body:
Dead code that will never execute\: attempting to add a streaming beta header in the non\-streaming `doGenerate` method where `body.stream` is always falsy\.
View Details
📝 Patch Details ```diff diff --git a/packages/anthropic/src/anthropic-messages-language-model.ts b/packages/anthropic/src/anthropic-messages-language-model.ts index b80ff9764..f669e5ca9 100644 --- a/packages/anthropic/src/anthropic-messages-language-model.ts +++ b/packages/anthropic/src/anthropic-messages-language-model.ts @@ -569,14 +569,6 @@ export class AnthropicMessagesLanguageModel implements LanguageModelV3 { userSuppliedBetas: await this.getBetasFromHeaders(options.headers), }); - // Enable fine-grained tool streaming beta when streaming + enabled - const providerToolStreaming = - options.providerOptions?.anthropic?.toolStreaming ?? true; - - if (body.stream && providerToolStreaming) { - betas.add('fine-grained-tool-streaming-2025-05-14'); - } - // Extract citation documents for response processing const citationDocuments = this.extractCitationDocuments(options.prompt); ```
### Analysis ## Dead code\: unreachable streaming beta header in doGenerate\(\) **What fails\:** `doGenerate()` method in `anthropic-messages-language-model.ts` lines 572\-578 contains unreachable code attempting to conditionally add the `fine-grained-tool-streaming-2025-05-14` beta header based on `body.stream`\, but this value is always falsy \(undefined\) in this context\. **How to reproduce\:** The dead code is at lines 572\-578\: ```typescript // Enable fine-grained tool streaming beta when streaming + enabled const providerToolStreaming = options.providerOptions?.anthropic?.toolStreaming ?? true; if (body.stream && providerToolStreaming) { betas.add('fine-grained-tool-streaming-2025-05-14'); } ``` **Root cause\:** * `doGenerate()` passes `stream: false` to `getArgs()` \(line 569\) * `getArgs()` returns `stream: stream === true ? true : undefined` \(line 462\) * Since `false === true` evaluates to false\, `body.stream` becomes `undefined` * The condition `if (body.stream && providerToolStreaming)` is always false because `body.stream` is falsy **Why this is a bug\:** The streaming beta is already correctly handled in `getArgs()` at line 422\: `if (stream && (anthropicOptions?.toolStreaming ?? true)) { betas.add('fine-grained-tool-streaming-2025-05-14'); }`\. This code in `doGenerate()` is redundant dead code that will never execute\. The fine\-grained tool streaming beta should only be enabled in `doStream()` \(which correctly passes `stream: true` to `getArgs()`\)\, not in `doGenerate()` which explicitly disables streaming\.

```suggestion
  public serverInfo!: ClientOrServerImplementation;
```

The `serverInfo` property is not initialized in the constructor but is declared as a required property\. This violates TypeScript\'s `strictPropertyInitialization` compiler option \(enabled via `strict: true` in the project\'s tsconfig\) and will cause a compilation error\.


<details>
<summary>View Details</summary>
<!-- PATCH_DETAILS_PLACEHOLDER -->

### Analysis
## TypeScript strict property initialization error on serverInfo

**What fails\:** Compilation fails with error TS2564 in `DefaultMCPClient` class\. The `serverInfo` property is declared on line 154 of `packages/mcp/src/tool/mcp-client.ts` without an initializer or definite assignment assertion\, violating TypeScript\'s `strictPropertyInitialization` compiler option\.

**How to reproduce\:**

```bash
cd packages/mcp
pnpm type-check
```

**Result\:**

```
src/tool/mcp-client.ts(154,10): error TS2564: Property 'serverInfo' has no initializer and is not definitely assigned in the constructor.
```

**Expected\:** Should compile successfully\. While `serverInfo` is assigned in the `init()` method at line 231 before the client is exposed to consumers\, TypeScript\'s static analysis cannot verify this control flow\. Adding a definite assignment assertion \(`!`\) signals to the compiler that this property will be initialized before use\.

**Fix\:** Added definite assignment assertion to the property declaration\:

```typescript
public serverInfo!: ClientOrServerImplementation;
```

This aligns with TypeScript best practices and the initialization pattern where `createMCPClient()` always awaits `init()` before returning the client instance\, ensuring `serverInfo` is initialized before any consumer access\.

</details>

body:
Changing from `unknown` to `any` reduces type safety and actually prevents type narrowing, contrary to the PR description's goal.

In TypeScript:
- `unknown` is the type-safe alternative that **requires** type narrowing before use, enabling discriminated union narrowing
- `any` bypasses the type system entirely and does **not** support type narrowing

If the goal is to enable "better type narrowing when using discriminated unions on `toolCall.input`", then `unknown` is the correct choice. The `any` type will allow any operation without type checking, which defeats the purpose of TypeScript's type system.

Consider keeping `unknown` or if there's a specific compatibility issue, please clarify the actual problem that `any` solves. Note that `DynamicToolCall` in `tool-call.ts` uses `input: unknown` (line 26), which suggests `unknown` is the intended type for dynamic tool inputs throughout the codebase.

The error handler in `wrapStream` doesn\'t remove the step from `activeSteps`\, causing a memory leak when stream\-related errors occur\.
View Details
📝 Patch Details ```diff diff --git a/packages/devtools/src/middleware.ts b/packages/devtools/src/middleware.ts index 2822e0da5..0b7029af5 100644 --- a/packages/devtools/src/middleware.ts +++ b/packages/devtools/src/middleware.ts @@ -371,6 +371,9 @@ export const devToolsMiddleware = (): LanguageModelV3Middleware => { ...rest, }; } catch (error) { + // Remove from active tracking - stream error occurred + activeSteps.delete(stepId); + const durationMs = Date.now() - startTime; await updateStepResult(stepId, { duration_ms: durationMs, ```
### Analysis ## Memory leak in wrapStream error handler when TransformStream methods throw **What fails\:** The error handler in `wrapStream()` \(packages\/devtools\/src\/middleware\.ts\, lines 362\-374\) doesn\'t remove steps from the `activeSteps` map when an error is thrown from TransformStream\'s `flush()` or `cancel()` methods\, causing the step to remain in memory indefinitely\. **How to reproduce\:** Create a scenario where the TransformStream\'s `flush()` or `cancel()` method throws an error\: ```javascript // When a stream encounters an error in flush/cancel that bubbles to the catch block, // the activeSteps.set() from line 252 is never paired with activeSteps.delete() // causing the step to persist in the map ``` **Result\:** Steps that encounter errors remain in `activeSteps` indefinitely\. When tested with an error thrown in `flush()`\, the step is not removed from the map\, and `activeSteps.size` remains 1 instead of being cleaned to 0\. Additionally\, during process termination \(lines 33\-60\)\, the signal handlers will process these orphaned steps again with a \"Request aborted\" error\, potentially overwriting the actual error that occurred\. **Expected\:** The `activeSteps.delete(stepId)` call should be executed before throwing the error\, matching the pattern used in the TransformStream\'s `flush()` \(line 331\) and `cancel()` \(line 350\) handlers\. **Fix applied\:** Added `activeSteps.delete(stepId);` to the catch block before error handling \(line 374\) to ensure the step is removed from tracking when stream\-related errors occur\.

```suggestion
    if (data && !data.error) {
      setSelectedRun(data);
    }
```

The `selectRun` function doesn\'t check if the fetch response is successful\, so if the API returns a 404 error \(when a run is deleted\)\, the error response object will be set as state and cause the component to crash when rendering code tries to access `selectedRun.steps` and `selectedRun.run`\.


<details>
<summary>View Details</summary>
<!-- PATCH_DETAILS_PLACEHOLDER -->

### Analysis
## Missing error handling in selectRun function allows crash when run is deleted

**What fails\:** The `selectRun()` function in `packages/devtools/src/viewer/client/app.tsx` \(line 352\) doesn\'t check for API errors before setting state\. When the API returns a 404 response with `{ error: 'Run not found' }`\, this error object is set as `selectedRun` state\, causing the component to crash when rendering code attempts to access properties like `selectedRun.steps` and `selectedRun.run`\.

**How to reproduce\:**

1.  Open the DevTools viewer and select a run
2.  Delete that run \(or make an API call to `/api/runs/{id}` that returns 404\)
3.  Component crashes with TypeError when trying to access `selectedRun.steps` or `selectedRun.run`

**What happens\:** TypeError exceptions at\:

*   Line 539\: `getFirstUserMessage(selectedRun.steps)` \- Cannot read property \'steps\' of error object
*   Line 541\: `selectedRun.run.isInProgress` \- Cannot read property \'run\' of error object
*   Line 557\: `selectedRun.steps.length` \- Cannot read property \'steps\' of error object
*   Line 570\: `selectedRun.run.started_at` \- Cannot read property \'run\' of error object

**Expected behavior\:** When the API returns an error response\, the `selectRun()` function should not update state with the error object\. The component should maintain its current state or clear the selected run gracefully\.

The API endpoint at `packages/devtools/src/viewer/server.ts` \(lines 98\-105\) returns `{ error: 'Run not found' }` with a 404 status code when a run doesn\'t exist\. The fix adds error checking before setting state\, matching the existing pattern in the SSE update handler \(lines 313\-322\) which already checks `if (data && !data.error)` before updating\.

</details>

🔧 Build Fix: The `simulate-streaming-middleware` attempts to enqueue `LanguageModelV3ToolApprovalRequest` as a stream part\, but this type is not assignable to `LanguageModelV3StreamPart`\. Tool approval requests are valid content but should not be streamed as parts\.
View Details
📝 Patch Details ```diff diff --git a/packages/ai/src/middleware/simulate-streaming-middleware.ts b/packages/ai/src/middleware/simulate-streaming-middleware.ts index d06cdadbe..7ae4a510d 100644 --- a/packages/ai/src/middleware/simulate-streaming-middleware.ts +++ b/packages/ai/src/middleware/simulate-streaming-middleware.ts @@ -51,6 +51,10 @@ export function simulateStreamingMiddleware(): LanguageModelMiddleware { id++; break; } + case 'tool-approval-request': { + // Tool approval requests are not valid stream parts and should not be enqueued + break; + } default: { controller.enqueue(part); break; ```
### Analysis ## TypeScript compilation error in simulate\-streaming\-middleware **What fails\:** TypeScript compiler fails with error TS2345 when building the DTS \(declaration types\) for the `ai` package\. **How to reproduce\:** ```bash cd packages/ai && pnpm run build ``` **Result\:** ``` src/middleware/simulate-streaming-middleware.ts(55,36): error TS2345: Argument of type 'LanguageModelV3Source | LanguageModelV3ToolCall | LanguageModelV3ToolResult | LanguageModelV3File | LanguageModelV3ToolApprovalRequest' is not assignable to parameter of type 'LanguageModelV3StreamPart | undefined'. Type 'LanguageModelV3ToolApprovalRequest' is not assignable to type 'LanguageModelV3StreamPart | undefined'. ``` **Root cause\:** The `simulate-streaming-middleware.ts` attempts to enqueue all content types from the generate result directly to a stream typed as `LanguageModelV3StreamPart`\. However\, `LanguageModelV3ToolApprovalRequest` is a valid content type but not a valid stream part type\, causing the TypeScript error\. **Fix\:** Added explicit handling to skip `tool-approval-request` content types in the switch statement since they should not be enqueued as stream parts\.
